tracks.title: Cincin Longgar
tracks.subject: a young goldsmith in a Pasar Atom Surabaya stall who resizes the same engagement ring three times because the customer's girlfriend's finger swells in the heat, until the man asks him to make it one size loose so it can stay on through every season

tracks.title: Angsa Es
tracks.subject: a hotel ice sculptor in Bandung who carves a swan for the breakfast buffet each dawn, watches it drip away by noon, and finally carves a swan small enough to melt in the palm of the pastry girl he loves

tracks.title: Titik Kumpul
tracks.subject: a volunteer fire warden in a Glodok electronics mall in an orange vest and helmet who shoos three hundred stall owners out in the monthly drill, and at the assembly point finds the phone-case girl counting heads and saying one person is still missing: him

tracks.title: Tabung Melon
tracks.subject: a 3-kilo gas cylinder deliveryman in a Bekasi rusun who carries one up four flights on his shoulder, paid in coins by every tenant and given tea by an old lady on the fourth floor, counting his steps like dance steps

tracks.title: Angka di Meteran
tracks.subject: a PLN electricity meter reader in a Malang lane who reads each household's life in its monthly numbers, and one month a long-silent house jumps overnight and he knocks to find the son who has come home

tracks.title: Empat Puluh Persen
tracks.subject: a Medan radio weather forecaster who every morning is phoned by listeners asking which forty percent of the city will get the rain, until he starts answering street by street

tracks.title: Sepatu Sekolah Ukuran Besar
tracks.subject: a shoe cobbler at a Kupang market who stitches a boy's school shoes with fishing line each term and secretly keeps the next size up on the shelf for him

tracks.title: Satu Dua Cha-cha-cha
tracks.subject: a 58-year-old man with two left feet who secretly pays for ten ballroom lessons so he can dance one proper cha-cha with his wife on their thirtieth anniversary

tracks.title: Telapak Tanganku Kosong
tracks.subject: a palm reader at a Yogyakarta night fair who tells every customer a bright future, and has never dared to read his own palm

tracks.title: Jendela Seberang
tracks.subject: a tower crane operator in Jakarta who sits forty metres up every morning and sees a woman across the street water her windowsill herbs, and finally lowers his hook with a note

tracks.title: Sabun Kecil dari Tiap Kota
tracks.mood: hangat, sabar, rindu yang tenang (warm, patient, quietly missing him)
tracks.subject: In their first rented house in Sidoarjo, a wife lines the bathroom shelf with the hotel soaps her husband, a travelling generator technician, brings home from every town, reads his month from the wrappers, and never unwraps the one from their honeymoon in Batu.

tracks.title: Kursi Tiga A
tracks.subject: On his first flight as co-pilot, a young Garuda pilot from Padang makes the cabin announcement and hears his own mother in seat 3A answer back, with fourteen relatives filling rows three to seven waving at the cockpit door.

tracks.title: Inyong Ora Gugup
tracks.subject: A Purwokerto graduate in a Jakarta job interview keeps her standard Indonesian polished until the interviewer slips, and he turns out to be from Cilacap, so she answers in ngapak and both of them laugh.

tracks.title: Turang, Geser Dulu
tracks.mood: riang, menggoda, bergoyang (cheerful, teasing, made for dancing)
tracks.subject: At a Kabanjahe kerja tahun, a Karo boy and his cousin turang, who by custom must open the landek together, plot to swap partners so each can dance with the person he or she actually likes.

tracks.title: Titik Akhir
tracks.subject: Two first-year chemistry students share one burette in a Pekanbaru campus lab; he keeps overshooting the endpoint to dark pink because he watches her instead of the drops, the assistant makes them start over until dusk, and she steadies his hand on the tap.

tracks.title: Struk di Dompetmu
tracks.subject: a woman in Depok who borrows her boyfriend's wallet for parking change and finds a folded stack of every minimarket coffee receipt from their first month together, which he has kept without telling her

tracks.title: Burung Kakatua Pak Udin
tracks.subject: a boy in Baubau who inherits an old cockatoo from the man next door who moved to Kendari, and the bird still calls only 'Udin, makan!' every evening, so the boy starts answering to Udin

tracks.title: Seragam Jangan Dicuci
tracks.subject: a girl on her last day of SMA whose white uniform shirt is covered in friends' marker signatures, hiding it in her cupboard so her mother will not put it in the wash

tracks.title: Cuma Bisa Tukar
tracks.subject: a man in Bandung trying to return a batik shirt two sizes too small for a refund, while the shop clerk keeps pointing at the sign saying exchange only and offering him every other shirt in the store

tracks.title: Gembul Diet
tracks.subject: a family in Kemayoran whose fat orange cat Gembul is put on a vet-ordered diet, and every member keeps secretly feeding him fried tempe until the next weigh-in shows he gained half a kilo

tracks.title: Setengah Cokelat Setengah Kacang
tracks.subject: a young couple in Bandung at midnight with money for only one martabak manis, arguing chocolate-cheese against peanut at the cart on Dago until they order it half and half and end up feeding each other the other side

tracks.title: Member Januari
tracks.genre: East Java sound horeg battle-bass DJ
tracks.subject: a man in Surabaya who signs up at a shophouse gym on the second of January, goes exactly once, and keeps paying the monthly auto-debit all year while the receptionist still waves at him by name

tracks.title: Botol Teh Mbak Sri
tracks.subject: a young man in Ngawi who drinks bottled tea every day to fill a sack for the kampung waste bank, just to stand at the Sunday scale while Mbak Sri, who runs it, weighs plastic and writes balances in her ledger without looking up

tracks.title: Jenderal di Atas Atap
tracks.genre: Indonesian late-80s slow rock power ballad
tracks.subject: a man in Tanah Abang keeping six chickens on his rooftop whose rooster Jenderal crows from the water tank at four every morning and wakes the whole gang, until the bubur seller thanks him for never being late

tracks.title: Saldo Kurang
tracks.subject: a young office worker at Tebet KRL station who keeps his commuter card balance low on purpose because the woman behind him at the ticket gate always taps him through with hers and lets him pay her back with a bottle of iced tea

tracks.title: Lewat Harmoni
tracks.subject: a Jakarta commuter on TransJakarta who teaches the woman standing beside him how to transfer at Harmoni from the Blok M line to the Kalideres line, every morning for two weeks, until one day they both stay on the bus past Harmoni on purpose

tracks.title: Pesanan Kopi Lantai Tujuh
tracks.subject: a first-job intern on the seventh floor of a Jakarta office whose only task for three weeks is photocopying, until his supervisor finally trusts him to take and place the whole office's afternoon coffee order

tracks.title: Kelas Memanjat
tracks.subject: a keeper at an orangutan rehabilitation centre in East Kalimantan who spends every morning of forest school coaxing one orphaned young orangutan off her back and onto a liana, counting the metres it climbs before it slides down to her again

tracks.title: Beo Pian
tracks.subject: a Banjarmasin man whose talking myna was meant to learn a pantun for the bird show, but only ever learned his wife's voice calling him home from the riverside coffee stall, and now shouts it at him in front of his friends

tracks.title: Huruf Nenek
tracks.subject: a young man in Makassar learning the Bugis lontara script letter by letter from a primary-school workbook so he can read the folded letters his grandmother sent him while he worked in a Malaysian palm-oil plantation, which he kept for six years without ever reading

tracks.title: Lampu Buah Naga
tracks.subject: a Banyuwangi dragon-fruit farmer who lights his field with yellow lamps from six till five to force off-season flowers, watches his electricity bill double, and ends up charging the courting teenagers who sneak in at night five thousand rupiah to take photos among the glowing poles

tracks.title: Gosok Bak Minum Dulu
tracks.subject: a Komodo keeper at Surabaya Zoo and the man who signs up as a Sunday volunteer because of her; she makes him scrub the water trough every Sunday for a month before she lets him hold the feeding pole

tracks.title: Laporan Jam Dua Pagi
tracks.subject: the night observer at the Merapi observation post in Kaliurang alone with the seismograph, counting avalanche quakes and phoning in the alert-level report to Yogyakarta, staged by himself as a one-man opera

tracks.title: Kantor Pos Taichung
tracks.subject: an Indonesian caregiver in Taichung spending her one Sunday off at the post office, where the parcel home to Cilacap is half a kilo over and she takes out her own new sandals so her son's school shoes still fit in the box

tracks.title: Motif Jengkol
tracks.genre: Indonesian late-60s beat pop (Koes Plus style)
tracks.subject: a cap stamper at a batik workshop in Pekalongan who presses the hot copper stamp four hundred times a day, ordered by the owner's wife to stamp her new design, a jengkol-bean motif, onto three hundred metres of cloth, which the town hall then picks as the Friday uniform, so the whole town wears his stinky-bean batik and he walks around deadpan proud

tracks.title: Tempa Lagi
tracks.subject: the youngest of five hammermen in a gong smithy in Wirun, Sukoharjo, forging a ninety-centimetre bronze gong ageng for a Solo dance school over three weeks of charcoal fire and hand hammers, under old Pak Darmo, who grips the red-hot disc in long tongs and keeps saying it will not sing yet, until the morning he strikes it once and sits down while the hum fills the shed

tracks.title: Regu Kancil
tracks.mood: bouncy, proud and a little cheeky
tracks.subject: a ten-year-old in scout troop Regu Kancil at his first Saturday-Sunday school scout camp, where the tent collapses before dark, the girls' troop next door mocks it, the instant noodles burn in the mess tin and his troop still wins the whistle morse-code game, whose message turns out to be 'take a bath'

tracks.title: Kartu Pos dari Tampere
tracks.mood: shy, sweet and a little comic
tracks.subject: a young Pos Indonesia courier in Malang who delivers Postcrossing postcards from Finland, Taiwan, Belarus and Germany to the same woman every Tuesday, reads them at the red light, and finally buys a card at his own post office counter to invite her for coffee, which he then has to deliver himself

tracks.title: Lima Sembilan
tracks.subject: a woman ham-radio operator on her Bekasi rooftop through the forty-eight-hour CQ World Wide contest, logging stations from Osaka to Rio and Alaska and giving every one of them the same 'five-nine' signal report, while her husband, who grumbles about the cracked roof tiles, brings up her rice and then spends the night replacing those tiles by torchlight under her antenna

tracks.title: Lutut Kanan
tracks.subject: a forty-one-year-old former second-division striker nicknamed Si Kijang, hired for three hundred thousand rupiah a match to play for a village team in an inter-kampung tarkam tournament on a harvested rice field, his right knee strapped, kicked by nineteen-year-old defenders, until the ball bounces off the bad knee into the net

tracks.title: Kaos Keramat
tracks.subject: a Persib supporter in Bandung who has not washed his knock-off blue jersey through nine unbeaten home games, while his boarding-house mates leave cream detergent outside his door

tracks.title: Padel Jam Enam
tracks.subject: four girlfriends on a six a.m. padel court in South Jakarta, three of them there for the photos and the narrator there to win

tracks.title: Dadak Merak
tracks.subject: a young pembarong in Ponorogo training to hold the fifty-kilogram dadak merak peacock mask by his teeth, three weeks before the Grebeg Suro festival

tracks.title: Bas deng Melodi
tracks.subject: a married couple in a Tomohon church kolintang group, she on the melody bars at one end of the row and he on the bass box at the other, cueing each other across the hall at Thursday rehearsals

tracks.title: Sarapan di Bibir Kawah
tracks.subject: a Rinjani porter from Sembalun cooking banana pancakes on the crater rim at dawn while his trekkers go up to the summit

tracks.title: Nunggu Nasi Matang
tracks.subject: a couple dancing in their narrow rented kitchen while waiting for the rice cooker to click over to warm

tracks.title: Kolong Banjir
tracks.subject: riders pushing stalled motorbikes through a flooded underpass while a politician's smiling billboard hangs above them

tracks.title: Topping Dobel
tracks.subject: a martabak manis seller in a Bekasi night street stall who argues with every customer that chocolate-cheese-peanut-condensed-milk is too much, then makes it anyway

tracks.title: Minyak Wangi Tanah Abang
tracks.subject: a perfume-oil seller in Tanah Abang market who can mix a bottle to match any smell a customer describes

tracks.title: Layangan Tujuh Belas
tracks.subject: a kampung kite maker who builds a three-metre kite for the Seventeenth of August contest and the whole street takes turns holding the line in the rice field

tracks.title: Sound Horeg Pak RT
tracks.mood: rowdy, sleepless and laughing about it
tracks.subject: a neighbourhood head's son testing a rented stack of sound-system speakers at two in the morning before a wedding, and the windows rattle until the whole alley comes out and dances

tracks.title: Gitar Dijual
tracks.subject: a student selling his guitar to pay the boarding-house rent, and the buyer, a high-school kid, asks him to play one last song before taking it

tracks.title: Transit Manggarai
tracks.genre: Indonesian art rock with tribal percussion
tracks.subject: changing trains at Manggarai station at seven in the morning, pushed up the stairs by the crowd while holding a box of birthday cake for a colleague

tracks.title: Lagu Buat Eyang
tracks.subject: a man learning an old keroncong song on a borrowed ukulele for six weeks to sing at his girlfriend's grandmother's eightieth birthday, so the family will take him seriously

tracks.title: Kabut Sikunir
tracks.subject: riding a motorbike up to Sikunir hill on the Dieng plateau at four in the morning with a friend to see the sunrise, and seeing nothing but white fog

tracks.title: Di Bawah Helm
tracks.mood: tired and quietly grateful, swelling into a full room singing back
tracks.subject: an ojek driver who works Sundays and listens to the sermon on one earbud in the church car park between rides, singing the closing worship song under his helmet while he waits for the next order

tracks.title: Tiga Ratus Petir
tracks.mood: giddy and breathless, a festival-night rush
tracks.subject: the girl at a festival's glitter face-paint booth who paints the same lightning bolt on three hundred faces before the headliner, then paints one on herself and runs for the main stage

tracks.title: Gerbang Jam Sepuluh
tracks.mood: bratty, gleeful and built to be shouted back
tracks.subject: climbing the locked boarding-house gate at eleven at night after a gig while the landlady waits on the porch with a flashlight

tracks.title: Bentar Lagi Jalan
tracks.mood: exasperated and bouncing, laughing through the wait
tracks.subject: a new employee stuck in an empty angkot at the terminal while the driver waits for it to fill up and keeps saying it is leaving any minute

tracks.title: Pinjol
tracks.genre: classic dangdut, Soneta-style orkes Melayu rock
tracks.mood: a comic cautionary tale, scolding with a wink
tracks.subject: a man who took an online loan to buy a new phone, and the debt collector messages everyone in his contacts, starting with his mother-in-law

tracks.title: Balak Enam
tracks.mood: comic and swaying, a sly village tall tale
tracks.subject: three men on the village ronda night-watch post who are meant to patrol and spend the night arguing over a game of gaple, while a chicken thief walks past behind them

tracks.title: Antre Bimbingan
tracks.subject: falling for the girl who waits in the same thesis-supervision queue outside a lecturer's office every Tuesday

tracks.title: Katanya
tracks.mood: wry and scolding, a sisterly telling-off
tracks.subject: the neighbourhood WhatsApp group forwarding a warning about a kidnapper disguised as a balloon seller, and the whole street chasing Pak Udin, who has sold balloons there for twenty years

tracks.title: Panjat Pinang
tracks.subject: a young man climbing the greased pole at the Independence Day contest to win the bicycle prize for the girl across the alley, sliding down every time while she heckles him in pantun

tracks.title: Lampu Cumi
tracks.subject: a squid-fishing crew stringing green lamps on their boat and racing the other boats out of Indramayu harbour at dusk

tracks.title: Masih Login
tracks.mood: furious, spiteful, built for a crowd to shout back
tracks.subject: an ex who still logs into his streaming account three months after the breakup

tracks.title: Oleng
tracks.mood: flirty and teasing, a settled couple showing off for each other
tracks.subject: a couple on a rented tandem bike at Jakarta's Sunday car-free day on Sudirman, she pedalling hard from the back, he steering badly from the front, stopping for ketoprak by the roundabout

tracks.title: Coret Aja
tracks.mood: giddy, rowdy and proud, a lump in the throat underneath
tracks.subject: the last day of SMA, when the whole class scribbles signatures and jokes on each other's white uniforms with markers and the homeroom teacher pretends to disapprove, then signs a sleeve himself

tracks.title: Helm Pink
tracks.mood: wounded and pleading, with a sting at the end
tracks.subject: seeing his girlfriend at a red light on the back of another man's motorbike, wearing the pink helmet he bought her

tracks.title: Imam Dadakan
tracks.subject: being pushed forward to lead the Maghrib prayer in the office prayer room during overtime because the usual imam is on leave

tracks.title: Titip Kunci
tracks.mood: dignified release that builds to defiance
tracks.subject: leaving the spare key to his apartment with the night security guard instead of returning it face to face

tracks.title: Mangga Tetangga
tracks.mood: santuy, a whole afternoon spent waiting for one mango
tracks.subject: waiting all afternoon under the neighbour's overhanging mango tree because, by kampung custom, fruit that falls on your side is yours

tracks.title: Foto KTP
tracks.subject: begging the clerk at the subdistrict office to retake an ID card photo snapped mid-sneeze

tracks.title: Prit, Dua Ribu
tracks.mood: deadpan fury you can dance to
tracks.subject: the parking attendant who appears from nowhere to whistle you out of a minimarket lot and charge two thousand rupiah

tracks.title: Sandal Jepit
tracks.mood: tender and warmly amused, ten years into a marriage
tracks.subject: a husband giving his wife his own flip-flops when her strap snaps on the walk home from the night fair, and walking the last kilometre barefoot

tracks.title: Bakar Ikan
tracks.mood: a family with only one question
tracks.subject: grilling skipjack on an Ambon beach with every cousin who came home

tracks.title: Supir Truk Pantura
tracks.mood: twenty years of road and one phone call
tracks.subject: a cement truck driver on the north coast road who stops for his son's phone call

tracks.title: Marga
tracks.mood: instant family in a city of strangers
tracks.subject: finding your own clan name on a stranger's business card in Jakarta

tracks.title: Pohon Beringin
tracks.mood: a village that will not lift the axe
tracks.subject: the old banyan at the edge of the village standing on the red line of a road map

tracks.title: Merantau
tracks.genre: pop Minang with saluang and talempong
tracks.mood: the custom that never says how to wave
tracks.subject: a son leaving Bukittinggi to merantau and his father checking the motorbike tyres three times

tracks.title: Setrika Seragam
tracks.mood: doing the one thing you can actually fix
tracks.subject: ironing a child's school uniform at nine every night

tracks.title: Tukang Bakso Lewat
tracks.mood: a clock made of somebody else's labour
tracks.subject: the meatball cart that has passed at half past seven for thirteen years

tracks.title: Arisan
tracks.genre: Sundanese pop with kacapi and suling
tracks.mood: the real reason nobody says out loud
tracks.subject: twelve women, one jar, and the two hours a month nobody tells them to stand up

tracks.title: Mudik
tracks.mood: the cheapest trade you ever make
tracks.subject: fourteen hours on the road once a year to become somebody's child again

tracks.title: Jam Dinding Telat Lima Menit
tracks.mood: keeping a fault because it is his
tracks.subject: the wall clock that has been five minutes slow since childhood

tracks.title: Golongan Darah O
tracks.subject: donating blood because there happened to be a banner outside the office

tracks.title: mama belum hafal sandinya
tracks.subject: teaching your mother to use the mobile banking app

tracks.title: Lakban Jam Satu
tracks.subject: packing eighty-three parcels alone at one in the morning

tracks.title: Dua Puluh Lima
tracks.subject: twenty-five years of marriage, noticing a burn scar on a hand

tracks.title: Kulkas Naik Tangga
tracks.subject: a flood morning, carrying the refrigerator up seventeen steps

tracks.title: Gajian Hari Jumat
tracks.subject: gajian dipakai habis dalam semalam

tracks.title: Lembur Lagi
tracks.subject: lembur tanpa dibayar

tracks.title: Maaf Yang Keberapa
tracks.subject: minta maaf yang kesekian kali

tracks.title: Ngomong Jowo Neng Kene
tracks.subject: bicara bahasa daerah di Jakarta

tracks.title: Jam Tiga Belum Pulang
tracks.subject: dugem sampai pagi karena nggak mau pulang

tracks.title: Hati Yang Tetap Menunggu
tracks.persona: a vocalist backed by a small horn section
tracks.subject: a long-distance call
